stance_basis: SEWRPC's regional plans explicitly recommend the Airport Spur and its clearinghouse approved the project as conforming to regional transportation plans
summary: SEWRPC is the regional planning commission whose adopted land use and transportation plans for 1990 explicitly recommend connecting General Mitchell Field to Interstate Route I-94 by a four-lane divided freeway, forming a key planning basis for the Airport Spur project. SEWRPC provided A-95 Clearinghouse approval confirming the Airport Spur conforms to the regional transportation plan and Milwaukee County Jurisdictional Highway System Plan. SEWRPC is also actively involved in related planning efforts including the regional air quality maintenance plan and regional airport systems plan, all of which support the project's context.
complaint_summary: SEWRPC provided A-95 Clearinghouse approval on January 1, 1971, confirming that the Airport Spur is in conformance with the regional transportation plan and Milwaukee County Jurisdictional Highway System Plan.
summary_quote: In light of the planning history related to the Airport Spur, the existence of other freeways already within the vicinity, the presence of airport and air generated ground and air travel, and the transitioning of land uses from agricultural to residential and industry in the vicinity of the airport, it is difficult to find that the Airport Spur will have an adverse environmental impact on the community which has already been subject to or constructed around major transportation facilities.

mentions.quote: According to the SEWRPC the studies completed to date indicates that the elimination of automotive congestion through highway construction is an effective means of reducing the total emissions of carbon monoxide and hydrocarbons within the region.

SEMRPC's Regional Land Use-Transportation Plan for 1990, the refined Jurisdictional Highway System Plan for Milwaukee County-1990, and the Milwaukee Area Transit Plan all recommended a bus rapid transit system for the Milwaukee Metropolitan Area.

In light of the planning history related to the Airport Spur, the existence of other freeways already within the vicinity, the presence of airport and air generated ground and air travel, and the transitioning of land uses from agricultural to residential and industry in the vicinity of the airport, it is difficult to find that the Airport Spur will have an adverse environmental impact on the community which has already been subject to or constructed around major transportation facilities.

Spokesman for SEWRPC read a prepared statement indicating the Airport Spur is sound, in the public interest, and in accord with the long-range land use and transportation system development plans prepared by SEWRPC and urged for it's construction.
